identity.title: WizardMath: Empowering Mathematical Reasoning for Large Language Models via Reinforced Evol-Instruct

problem.claim: Improve large language models’ mathematical reasoning abilities.

gap.claim: Most existing open-source models are pretrained on large-scale internet data without math-related optimization.

contributions.claim: Introduces WizardMath, applying Reinforcement Learning from Evol-Instruct Feedback (RLEIF) to mathematics.
Reports strong performance for WizardMath across the GSM8k and MATH mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
Preliminarily identifies instruction evolution and process supervision as important to exceptional math performance.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper’s stated distinction is applying the proposed RLEIF method to the math domain to enhance LLM mathematical reasoning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that WizardMath-Mistral 7B surpasses all other open-source LLMs by a substantial margin.
The authors report that WizardMath 70B outperforms ChatGPT-3.5, Claude Instant, Gemini Pro, and Mistral Medium.
A preliminary exploration reported by the authors highlights instruction evolution and process supervision as pivotal for exceptional math performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs have shown strong performance on challenging mathematical reasoning tasks.
Most open-source models lack math-related optimization after internet-scale pretraining.
WizardMath applies RLEIF to the mathematics domain.
Experiments on GSM8k and MATH report strong results, including open-source and broader model comparisons.
Preliminary exploration emphasizes instruction evolution and process supervision.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a domain-specific training method with a preliminary account of which components support performance: instruction evolution and process supervision.

lessons.interpretation: A concise abstract can connect the proposed intervention to an explanatory decomposition, while distinguishing preliminary analysis from benchmark evidence.
lessons.application: When presenting a specialized training method, separately report task performance and an explicitly qualified analysis of which design components may matter.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the study contains no component analysis or when the abstract cannot support a qualified explanation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark scores, evaluation protocols, baselines beyond named models, or statistical uncertainty.
The meaning and implementation of RLEIF, instruction evolution, and process supervision are not detailed.
The basis and scope of the reported model comparisons are unspecified.
